newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SHARES SEEN DOWN ON BEARISH SENTIMENT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SHARES SEEN DOWN ON BEARISH SENTIMENT.

text.p: Hungarian shares are expected to move down on Monday, dragged lower by the Wall Street's losses and the dollar's weakness against the forint, traders said.
"The Dow Jones shows direction as to what to expect," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft. "There was a minor (upward) correction on Friday, but now one can see that the trend is bearish."

Of Central Europe's bourses, Budapest is the most correlated to Wall Street due to the high proportion of foreign investors, and tends to follow moves of the U.S. market in the absence of substantial domestic corporate or macroeconomic news.
The dollar's current weakness against the forint also points to a decline in the BUX index as a weaker dollar generally makes the forint and thus Hungarian shares more expensive to foreign investors.
Tamas Revesz of Wintrust also said after recent peaks the market was entering a phase of downward correction.
"The market has accepted there is a correction underway and investors do not fear selling," he said.
Traders said chemicals TVK might resist the market's likely fall after Friday's block deal in which state privatisation agency APV sold its remaining stake in the company
On Friday the BUX index finished at 7,799.02 points, up up 57.27 points.
